facts.statement: Schleitheimia is an extinct sauropodiform sauropodomorph dinosaur named after its type locality in Switzerland.
facts.quote: Schleitheimia (named after the type locality of Schleitheim), is an extinct genus of sauropodiform sauropodomorph dinosaur, from the Gruhalde Member of Klettgau Formation of Switzerland.

facts.statement: The type material for Schleitheimia was collected between 1952 and 1954 by Emil Schutz.
facts.quote: The type material was collected between 1952 and 1954 by Emil Schutz.

facts.statement: The collected remains were donated to the University of Zürich in 1955.
facts.quote: They were donated to the University of Zürich in 1955.

facts.statement: In 1986, Peter Galton described most of the material and referred it to the species Plateosaurus engelhardti.
facts.quote: In 1986, most of the material was described by Peter Galton, who referred them all to the species Plateosaurus engelhardti.

facts.statement: Oliver Rauhut, Femke Holwerda, and Heinz Furrer redescribed the remains in 2020, including new finds from a 2016 excavation.
facts.quote: In 2020, Oliver Rauhut, Femke Holwerda and Heinz Furrer redescribed most of Schutz's remains, as well as some remains in the collections of the Museum zu Allerheiligen in Schaffhausen and new remains from an excavation in 2016 led by Holwerda.

facts.statement: The researchers named the new genus and species Schleitheimia schutzi to honor the type locality and the original discoverer.
facts.quote: They found that the earlier found remains represented a new genus and species, which they named Schleitheimia schultzi, honoring the type locality and the discoverer of the type remains.

facts.statement: The holotype, PIMUZ A/III 550, is a partial right ilium found in a Norian-aged layer of the Klettgau Formation.
facts.quote: The holotype, PIMUZ A/III 550, was found in a layer of the Klettgau Formation dating from the Norian. It consists of a partial right ilium.

facts.statement: The holotype of Schleitheimia displays several unique derived traits known as autapomorphies.
facts.quote: The holotype of Schleitheimia shows a number of autapomorphies, unique derived traits.

facts.statement: The fourth trochanter of the ilium in Schleitheimia is very robust.
facts.quote: The fourth tronchanter of the ilium is very robust.

facts.statement: The crista tibiofibularis of the femur is broad and lacks a posteriorly facing shelf lateral to it.
facts.quote: The crista tibiofibularis of the femur is broad and there is no posteriorly facing shelf is present lateral to the crista.

facts.statement: Schleitheimia is classified within the superorder Dinosauria, order Saurischia, suborder Sauropodomorpha, and unranked family Massopoda.
facts.quote: superordo: Dinosauria ordo: Saurischia subordo: Sauropodomorpha unranked_familia: Massopoda unranked_genus: Sauropodiformes

facts.statement: Schleitheimia lived during the Norian stage of the Triassic, between 227.3 and 205.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Norian to Norian (227.3 to 205.7 million years ago)
